passages.text: Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like contentment. When you’re contented, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.
passages.note: Contentment as the ground of goodness

passages.text: Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like good friends. When you have good friends, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.
Loss of wealth, mendicants, is a small thing. Wisdom is the worst thing to lose.
passages.note: Financial loss weighed against losing wisdom

passages.text: Loss of fame, mendicants, is a small thing. Wisdom is the worst thing to lose.
passages.note: Losing reputation or status in perspective
